title: Decoupled SLI telemetry bus and admit-throttling visualization
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a decoupled telemetry bus for SLIs that lets downstream consumers (dashboards, runbooks, synthetic probes) subscribe to token-granular latency and admit events without adding tail latency to serving paths. This ticket builds the telemetry bus, wire-up for token-level p50/p95/p99 SLIs, and a new admit-throttling dashboard that visualizes admission score distributions, shed decisions, regional spillovers, and circuit state transitions.

Problem statement:
- Current in-process SLI aggregation increases tail latency and couples the instrumenter with serving.
- Observability consumers (dashboards, chaos harness, failover playbooks) need richer tokenized traces and admit decision contexts (kv_hit, prefix_len, priority) to diagnose cascading sheds across regions.
- We lack a compact subscription mechanism for sampling high-cardinality token telemetry without overloading storage/ingest.

Goals:
1) Implement an out-of-band SLI telemetry bus (Kafka-compatible stream) that service nodes publish lightweight admit and token-latency events to (protobuf envelope).
2) Provide a consumer library (python/go) that materializes per-route token SLI rollups and exposes sliding-window p50/p95/p99 and admitted_rate metrics to Prometheus/OTLP.
3) Build an admit-throttling dashboard in Grafana that includes: admit score histogram, KV cache hit vs latency correlation, per-region shed rate, circuit state timeline, and synthetic-probe alignment panel.
4) Add controlled sampling logic for tokens (adaptive reservoir with priority bias) to cap telemetry volume under load while preserving tail signal.

Scope / Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change SLO thresholds themselves (handled in PM follow-up).
- Does not migrate all existing SLI consumers; starts with console and chaos harness as first consumers.

Implementation notes:
- Telemetry envelope fields: request_id, route, tenant_id (hashed), shard_id, sequence_len_bucket, token_index, token_latency_ms, kv_hit (bool), admit_score (float), admit_decision (admit/reject/early_exit), timestamp, region, model_variant. Keep envelope < 600 bytes.
- Use a ring-buffered producer in the serving runtime and an async IO thread to publish to the bus; producer should backpressure locally to the admit controller but not block decode path—drop non-critical telemetry when ring full.
- Consumer pipeline will aggregate per-route sliding windows (30s, 5m, 1h) and emit Prometheus histograms + p95 gauge derived from histogram.
- Sampling: reservoir with two strata — a) priority tokens (high-cost requests, errored requests) always sampled up to N/s, b) background reservoir for uniform sampling. Configure per-tenant caps.
- Privacy: tenant_id must be hashed and only last-8 hex retained. No PII.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime changes compile and pass integration tests; telemetry producer has <1% additional tail error budget in canary.
- Consumer library produces sliding-window p95/p99 gauges and Prometheus histograms for route/region within a minute of ingestion.
- Grafana dashboard panels implemented and linked: admit_score_histogram, kvhit_vs_token_p95_heatmap, region_spillover_flow, circuit_transition_timeline. Dashboard reviewed by PM and Observability lead.
- Sampling controls exposed via feature flags and per-tenant config in console.
- Chaos harness (ENG-412992) consumes the new telemetry and uses it to validate failover behavior in two regions.

Tasks:
- [ ] Define telemetry protobuf schema and size constraints (runtime).
- [ ] Implement ring-buffered async producer in runtime (C++/Rust depending on service) with opt-out compile flag.
- [ ] Add adaptive reservoir sampler to runtime and config knobs (rate limits, priority biases).
- [ ] Build Go consumer that folds token events into Prometheus histograms (inc. sliding windows).
- [ ] Instrument console ingestion path to accept new SLI metrics and update rollups.
- [ ] Grafana dashboard buildout and initial panels (link below).

Risks and mitigations:
- High cardinality → implement reservoir + hashed tenant buckets and strict envelope schema.
- Runtime overhead → ring-buffer and opt-out, validate in canary and limit telemetry per-node.
- Data loss during failover → consumer must be resilient; implement short-retention local buffer + at-least-once ingest semantics; consumers dedupe on request_id.

Notes and links to artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Decoupled+SLI+Telemetry+Bus (internal)
- Telemetry protobuf draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/telemetry/proto/v1/telemetry.proto
- Consumer prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/482
- Runtime producer sketch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1938
- Grafana draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/AdmitThrottling/admit-throttle-v1
- Chaos harness that will consume this: ENG-412992

Owner notes:
- Start with console and chaos harness consumers, then onboard console alerts and runbook triggers in a follow-up.
- Coordinate with security for hashed tenant_id pattern and with privacy to confirm no PII leakage.
acceptance_criteria: Producer added to runtime and compiled in canary with <=1% additional tail error budget
Go consumer produces sliding-window p95/p99 gauges and Prometheus histograms per route and region
Grafana admit-throttling dashboard has required panels and is reviewed by PM/Observability
Sampling knobs exposed and can limit telemetry to configured per-tenant caps
Chaos harness (ENG-412992) consumed telemetry and validated multi-region shed scenarios in staging
